title: Challenge: debug a container that has no shell
intro: Your pod 'app' runs a distroless image, tiny and secure, but it has no shell, no ls, nothing to debug with. `kubectl exec` is useless here. Ephemeral debug containers to the rescue. (Commands checked; output illustrative.)

steps.instruction: First, see the problem: try to get a shell in the 'app' pod.
steps.success: OCI runtime exec failed: exec failed: unable to start container process: exec: "sh": executable file not found in $PATH   <- distroless has no shell
steps.fail: Try kubectl exec -it app -- sh (it will fail, that's the point).

steps.instruction: Attach an ephemeral debug container (busybox) that shares the process namespace of the 'app' container.
steps.success:
Defaulting debug container name to debugger-7x2k.
If you don't see a command prompt, try pressing enter.
/ #   <- you're in a busybox shell, alongside the app's processes
steps.fail: Use kubectl debug with -it, an --image (e.g. busybox), and --target=app so it shares the namespace.

steps.instruction: From the debug container, list processes to see the app running (it shares the PID namespace).
steps.success:
PID   USER   TIME  COMMAND
    1 root   0:00  /app/server --port 8080
   14 root   0:00  ps aux   <- there's your distroless app (PID 1)
steps.fail: List the running processes (e.g. ps aux).

done: Solved! `kubectl debug --target` injects a throwaway container into a running pod, sharing its namespaces, so you can inspect distroless or scratch containers that ship with nothing. The app image stays minimal; debugging tools come and go on demand.
